title: Sub-Scope Index Architecture
summary: propose collection identity, shared report ownership, manage-only contributions, selection lifecycle, and explicit function adoption for docs_subscope
content_html:
Sub-Scope Index Architecture

Proposed Outcome

docs_subscope becomes the generic collection index for a configured one-level sub-scope. It retains one shared public-safe list/detail reader, while the manage entrypoint contributes optional controls and workflows without loading their modules on public routes.

The report remains the owner of collection rendering and navigation. Management workflows remain owned by the management host and validated local services. This is a focused extension contract for docs_subscope, not a general conversion of reports into dashboards or write surfaces.

Collection Identity

The browser and services should share one normalized collection model:

parent collection:    { scope }
sub-scope collection: { scope, sub_scope }

document target:      { scope, doc_id }
                  or  { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }

selection target:     collection + checked doc_ids

sub_scope identifies one configured child collection. It is not a top-level scope alias, an arbitrary source path, or a route-selected namespace.

Raw child doc_id values are unique only inside their owning { scope, sub_scope }. Every cache key, request, activity record, package metadata record, or action handoff that crosses the report boundary must retain that collection identity.

Shared Report Ownership

The shared docs_subscope report owns:

  • validating the configured sub-scope;
  • loading the public manifest or supplied local inventory;
  • list ordering and row/detail rendering;
  • subdoc URL state and Back/Forward behavior;
  • membership and by-ID payload identity validation;
  • the currently validated detail target;
  • contained unavailable and failure states; and
  • optional list-row, list-toolbar, and detail-toolbar contribution hosts.

The shared report does not own:

  • management capability checks;
  • checkbox selection state;
  • management action definitions or dispatch;
  • preview/apply mutation workflows;
  • package preparation;
  • Tag Registry reads or writes; or
  • public promotion of management data.

An extension host should exist only when the caller supplies a contribution. Public mode therefore receives neither an empty management toolbar nor an import path to its implementation.

Public And Manage Projections

Public mode keeps the existing minimal collection contract:

{"doc_id": "<id>", "title": "<title>"}

Manage mode supplies one compact inventory containing:

{
  "doc_id": "<id>",
  "title": "<title>",
  "ui_status": "<status>",
  "viewable": true
}

The compact inventory supports collection rendering. Full source metadata and body content remain exact-document reads. The report must not issue one full record request per row.

Status and non-viewable icons remain local projections from the manage inventory. A missing ui_status remains a valid no-icon state unless a later UI decision introduces an explicit unclassified icon.

Rows and actions use doc_id as identity. Title remains display data; this feature introduces no title-uniqueness, collision, or deduplication contract.

Row Presentation

Status and non-viewable icons prefix the title text inside the title cell, matching the main Index. They are part of the displayed title treatment, not separate columns or canonical title data. Their icons remain hidden from assistive technology while the title control's accessible name includes the corresponding status labels.

Checkboxes occupy a dedicated first cell or column before the title. Each checkbox remains a sibling of the title navigation control so selection cannot also navigate or create nested interactive controls. The checkbox cell is contributed only in manage selection mode and is omitted or collapsed otherwise; public rows remain title-only and load no selection module.

selection mode:  [checkbox] [status icon + non-viewable icon + title]
ordinary/public:            [status icon + non-viewable icon + title]

Manage-Only Contribution

A focused manage-owned controller should contribute:

  • a detail toolbar mounted only for a validated detail target;
  • a list toolbar for collection actions and selection commands;
  • a dedicated sibling checkbox cell before each list-row title;
  • collection-local selection projection and event handling;
  • capability-aware action state;
  • lazy workflow loading; and
  • refresh/reconciliation after a committed collection mutation.

The shared report should pass explicit hosts, records, and validated targets. Management code should not infer targets from subdoc, scrape private report markup, or fall back to the selected parent document.

Presentation for these controls belongs in the manage stylesheet. Public CSS may retain only the shared report layout required for public reading.

Selection Lifecycle

Index and sub-scope selection should reuse the same pure transition rules but have separate owners.

The sub-scope owner is keyed by { scope, sub_scope } and owns:

  • selection mode;
  • checked IDs;
  • range anchor;
  • Select all, Clear, and Done;
  • pruning after inventory refresh or deletion; and
  • exit when the report unmounts, the collection changes, or management mode is left.

Opening a detail and returning to the same mounted collection may preserve the selection so a user can inspect a document without losing package preparation. Only checked IDs are supplied to selection actions. The displayed detail, focused row, URL subdoc, and selected parent index document are never fallback targets.

Checkboxes remain siblings of row navigation controls. Selecting a document for an action must not also navigate to its detail.

Function Adoption

Existing functions adopt sub-scope collections only when their complete contract can carry the collection identity:

function target proposed stance
list and detail read collection/document shipped baseline
source and metadata editing exact document shipped baseline
detail Delete exact validated document proposed
Prepare Package checked selection proposed, export-only first
returned-package Review/Import package/collection excluded until separately complete
scope settings, rename, lifecycle, publish top-level scope remain scope-only

This is a positive adoption model. The presence of sub_scope in one resolver does not make every scope action collection-aware.

Detail Delete

Delete is a rendered-detail control over one validated { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } target.

The management workflow should:

  1. request a write-free preview;
  2. show the exact source and generated consequences;
  3. require explicit confirmation;
  4. re-resolve and delete only the confined source document;
  5. rebuild the affected sub-scope outputs;
  6. clear the deleted subdoc with replacement history;
  7. refresh the local inventory and return to list state; and
  8. retain only blocker, unavailable-data, stale-state, and error feedback.

The mutation does not inspect or update Studio canonical data. Deleting a tag document may leave a stale Tag Registry doc_id, as defined by the independent association contract.

Normal success must not reload the parent index-tree, select another parent document, or redraw unrelated sidebar state.

Package Export

The existing Prepare Package workflow can remain the modal and export owner once its collection boundary is explicit.

Sub-scope adoption requires:

  • document-list reads scoped by { scope, sub_scope };
  • request and server validation that preserve sub_scope;
  • source loading from the configured child collection;
  • package metadata that records the complete collection identity;
  • checked-ID eligibility against that exact collection;
  • flat-collection profile behavior rather than assumed parent hierarchy; and
  • activity records that retain the collection target.

The first adoption should be export-only. Returned-package validation, review, canonical comparison, and import destinations would all need complete sub-scope support before a return-import profile could be truthful.

Independent Canonical Ownership

Sub-scope management acts only on Docs Viewer sources and projections.

  • It does not synchronize fields with Studio records.
  • It does not cascade Studio edits or deletes.
  • It does not prevent document deletion because an external record refers to the document.
  • It does not repair or infer external associations.
  • It may display or diagnose stale relationships through a separately owned feature.

This applies the Independent Canonical Documents concept without adding cross-application coupling to the report or Docs management service.

Risks And Pressure Points

  • A large flat collection may need report-owned search or filtering, but those controls require explicit list data and should not widen the public manifest accidentally.
  • Narrow layouts need explicit review once checkbox gutters and toolbars are present.
  • Direct detail Delete and future selection-backed bulk Delete are different interaction contracts and should not be conflated.
  • Collection refresh must reconcile local selection without reloading the parent index.
  • Public import-graph coverage must continue to reject manage-owned controllers, clients, workflows, and package modules.

Likely Authorities To Inspect

  • shared report: site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-subscope-report.js
  • manage bridge: docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-document-reports.js
  • managed target normalization and resolution: docs-viewer-management-document-target.js and docs_management_document_target.py
  • existing selection model and controller: docs-viewer-index-selection.js and docs-viewer-management-index-controller.js
  • package browser and service: docs-viewer/runtime/js/packages/ and docs-viewer/services/docs_document_packages/
  • local management routes, capability projection, mutation planning, and targeted rebuild services; and
  • focused public import-boundary, report-module, management-service, selection, and package tests.

These are inspection starting points. A delivery should confirm current ownership before naming exact changed files.

The feature parent owns review and later delivery navigation.
